newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Mobutu declares state of emergency.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu declares state of emergency.

text.p: Zaire's embattled president Mobutu Sese Seko declared a state of emergency on Tuesday in the teeming capital Kinshasa and throughout the rest of the Central African nation, over a third of which is under rebel control.
The veteran leader, who seized power in 1965 but has seen his hold over the sprawling country weakened by relentless rebel advances, announced the move on state television.
Mobutu told the television a state of emergency declared in the eastern provinces of North and South Kivu last year "is extended throughout the national territory".
He said five military governors had been appointed in provinces not held by the rebels, who took up arms in October vowing to topple him.
He did not make clear what restrictions would be imposed as part of the state of emergency or the implications for Kinshasa and its more than five million people.
Earlier, rebel leader Laurent Kabila told a rally in the diamond mining capital of Mbuji-Mayi that "elements" of his forces were in Bandundu, the last province before Kinshasa.
Members of Mobutu's presidential guard in Zaire's second city of Lubumbashi, like Kinshasa a declared rebel target, said that they had repulsed a rebel advance to the south of the city.
Mobutu returned to Kinshasa on March 21 from fresh cancer treatment in Europe. He had prostate cancer surgery in Switzerland in August.
